docs.text: Parting Placer Guide ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Parting Placer puts scalp partings on a head mesh in Blender. You place each parting with the mouse, then bake the result to texture maps. What It Does ¶ Each parting is one Empty plus one shader node group. The parting follows the surface of the head, and the mesh itself is never deformed. How A Parting Is Built explains more. Partings are a shader effect. You see them in Material Preview or Rendered shading. They do not show in Solid shading. Where To Start ¶ First time using the add-on? Start with Your First Parting In 10 Minutes . Looking up one button or setting? Go to the Panel Reference, starting at Panel Header . Something looks wrong? Check Troubleshooting . Where To Find The Panel ¶ The panel lives in the 3D Viewport sidebar. Press N , then select the Parting Placer tab. [1] The Parting Placer tab in the 3D Viewport sidebar Known Limitations ¶ Partings on the generated half of a Mirror modifier cannot be baked directly. That half shares its UVs with the real half. See Work On A Head With A Mirror Modifier . Freeze Layer works up to 3 times per material. The transparent export uses this head's UV layout, so it only fits this head. Coverage lost in a version before v1.1.0 cannot be recovered. See the Changelog . Support ¶ Email help@ebonix.com and include: your Blender version the add-on version, from Edit > Preferences > Add-ons what you did, what you expected, and what happened a screenshot of the panel and of the problem If the problem is in a baked map or an export, send the image itself. If You're Stuck No partings showing? See I Cannot See Any Partings . Nothing happens when you place? See Place Parting Does Nothing . Recommended next: Requirements And Compatibility

docs.text: Install, Update, Uninstall ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Install the add-on from its .zip file and find its panel in the 3D Viewport. You Need First The add-on .zip file from your purchase. A Blender version from Requirements And Compatibility . Install ¶ In Blender, open Edit > Preferences . Select Add-ons . Select the down arrow at the top right of the Add-ons section, beside Enabled Only . Select Install from Disk... . Pick the add-on .zip file. Enable Parting Placer Tool in the add-on list. In the 3D Viewport, press N to open the sidebar. Select the Parting Placer tab. [1] The Parting Placer tab after a fresh install Update ¶ Install the new version over the old one. You don't need to uninstall first. Open Edit > Preferences . Select Add-ons . Select the down arrow at the top right of the Add-ons section. Select Install from Disk... . Pick the new add-on .zip file. After updating, open each file that already has partings. Select Repair Partings once in that file. See Repair Partings . Uninstall ¶ Open Edit > Preferences . Select Get Extensions . Find Parting Placer Tool in the Installed list. Select the down arrow at the right of its row. Select Uninstall . Partings already in your files stay where they are and still show on the head. Without the add-on you can't edit them from the panel. If You're Stuck Still stuck after installing? See Still Stuck . docs.text: Your First Parting In 10 Minutes ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Place one parting on a head and bake it to texture maps you can use outside Blender. You Need First The add-on installed. See Install, Update, Uninstall . A head mesh with a material and a UV map. See Requirements . Your browser cannot play this clip. Read the steps as text . Placing one parting on a head, changing its colour and baking it Read the steps as text Set Up The Head (Steps 1 To 6 Of 23) ¶ Select your head mesh in the 3D Viewport. Press N to open the sidebar. Select the Parting Placer tab. Set Target to your head mesh. Press Z to open the shading menu. Select Material Preview . Partings only show in Material Preview or Rendered shading. Place A Parting (Steps 7 To 13 Of 23) ¶ Select Place Parting . Move the mouse over the head. A preview parting follows the cursor. Press S to switch to sizing. Scroll to resize the parting. Press S again to hand the scroll wheel back to the viewport. Left click to place the parting. Right click to finish. [1] The key guide in the viewport while you place A key guide sits in the viewport while you place. It lists each key and keeps the size, rotation and parting count up to date. Undo While Placing Press Ctrl+Z while placing to remove the last parting. After you finish, one Ctrl+Z undoes the whole session. All keys are listed on Place Parting And Placement Keys . Change Its Colour (Steps 14 To 16 Of 23) ¶ Select your parting in the parting list. In the Appearance block, select the Hair Color swatch. Pick a colour. With Link Appearance off, the Appearance heading names the parting you are editing. See Appearance . Bake And Save (Steps 17 To 23 Of 23) ¶ Select the triangle beside Bake to open the Bake block. Set Resolution to 1024 . Select Bake Partings . Wait for the bake to finish. Select Save Textures . Pick a folder in the file browser. Select Save Textures at the bottom right of the file browser. Normal Resolution keeps its own setting, 4096 by default. How long a bake takes depends on your computer and how many partings you have. Live Bump starts off, so this bake skips the Normal map. To get one, turn on Live Bump at the bottom of the Appearance block before you bake. A lower resolution bakes faster while you learn. Raise it for your final pass. Save Textures writes one PNG per baked map. Each file is named after the object, style, map and size, for example head_Style 1_Partings_Color_1024.png . If You're Stuck No parting showing? See I Cannot See Any Partings . Place Parting does nothing? See Place Parting Does Nothing . Bake Partings greyed out? See Bake Partings Is Greyed Out Or Refuses . Recommended next: Place Partings

docs.text: Straight Vs Premultiplied Alpha ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Two ways of storing colour in a see-through PNG. Leave Premultiplied off unless your game engine asks for it. Overview ¶ Straight alpha (Premultiplied off) keeps the full colour in every pixel, and stores how see-through it is separately. Even fully transparent pixels keep their colour. When an engine shrinks the texture for distance, the wrong colour can't bleed in at the edges. Premultiplied alpha (Premultiplied on) multiplies the colour by the transparency before saving. Some engines and pipelines expect this. In those, it gives correct edges. Elsewhere it gives up the protection straight alpha has. The setting only affects the file Save Transparent writes. It has nothing to do with the hidden pass the bake makes for the transparent export. That pass is always used and has no switch. If You're Stuck A pale edge round the partings? See The Transparent Export Has A Pale Or Skin-Coloured Edge . Recommended next: Export A Transparent Overlay

docs.text: How A Parting Is Built ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 A parting is a shading effect on your head's material, placed by an Empty. Your mesh is never changed. Overview ¶ Each parting has two parts: An Empty in your scene. It sets where the parting sits and which way it faces. You can select and move it like any other object. A shader node group in the head's material. It draws the parting image onto the head along the Empty's axes, so the parting follows the surface. The crown, sides and back all behave the same way. Because a parting is shading, you only see it in Material Preview or Rendered shading. In Solid shading it is invisible. The add-on works on a copy of your head's material. Its name ends in _Partings , for example Material.001_Partings . Your original material stays in the file. Each parting adds its own block of shader nodes to that material. That is why many live partings slow the viewport. See Live, Preview And Frozen Partings . If you delete an Empty by hand, its parting is left with nothing to place it. See Orphan Stamps Warning . If You're Stuck Can't see your partings? See I Cannot See Any Partings . Recommended next: Live, Preview And Frozen Partings

docs.text: Live, Preview And Frozen Partings ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 A parting can be in one of three states. Knowing which is which explains most viewport slowdowns. Overview ¶ State What it means How it gets there Live Drawn from scratch by Blender every time the material updates. Quick to edit, slow in large numbers. Every parting starts live. Preview Shown as a low-resolution stand-in. Fast, and nothing is lost. Enable Preview , or Auto Preview when you start placing. Frozen Baked into a checkpoint and taken out of the material for good. Bake Partings , then Freeze Layer . The number of live partings is what slows Blender down. Each parting adds its own block of shader nodes for Blender to process. Preview is the one to reach for first. It costs nothing, and Disable Preview brings full shading back. Freezing is for partings that are settled. You can freeze 3 times per material, and frozen work stays in your maps however many times you bake after. Baking alone does not change any state. After Bake Partings , every parting is still live. If You're Stuck The viewport is slow? See The Viewport Is Slow . Preview stayed on? See Preview Mode Is Still On After I Finish Placing . Recommended next: Keep The Viewport Fast

docs.text: Styles ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 A style is a complete set of partings on one head. Styles let you keep several looks on the same head and switch between them. Overview ¶ The first style on a head is called Style 1 . New Style… parks the current set and gives you an empty one to place into. Only one style shows on the head at a time. The others are parked, and their partings are kept in your file. Their Empties are hidden in a collection named after the head and the style, for example head - Style 1 . Each style keeps its own baked maps, so baking one style doesn't touch another's. Selecting a parked style loads it and parks the one that was showing. Turn Preview off before you switch. If You're Stuck Partings missing after switching? See I Cannot See Any Partings . Recommended next: Save And Switch Parting Styles

docs.text: What Baking Produces ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Baking turns your partings into image maps laid out on your head's UVs, ready to use outside Blender. Overview ¶ Map What it holds On by default Color The partings' colour over your head's own colour Yes Normal The fine bump detail. It has its own resolution, because it benefits from more pixels. Yes, but it only bakes while Live Bump is on. Live Bump starts off. Roughness How shiny or matte each spot is Yes Alpha Where the partings are, not what colour they are. Only needed for the transparent export. No With Color and Alpha both ticked, the bake also makes a hidden pass that only the transparent export uses. That is why Alpha costs two extra passes rather than one. You won't see that pass in the panel or in Save Textures . Baking again is safe. New maps carry the old ones forward, even across a change of resolution. A parting you delete is properly removed from the maps. Your partings stay live after a bake. To swap them for the baked images and delete their Empties, use Apply Bake . If You're Stuck Maps missing? See My Baked Maps Vanished . Holes in the maps? See Partings Bake With Small Holes In Them . Recommended next: Straight Vs Premultiplied Alpha

docs.text: Changelog ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 What changed in each version of the add-on, newest first. Each entry is tagged with the part of the panel it touches. V2.0.0 ¶ 27 October 2026. If you have partings in an existing file, run Repair Partings once after updating. Added Live Bump switch, in its own block at the bottom of Appearance. Bump costs the most when Blender rebuilds the material, so it now starts off and placing partings stays quick. Bump Strength and Bump Distance show when it is on. The block reminds you which way to set it: "Turn on when baking partings" while off, "Turn off whilst placing partings" while on. [panel: appearance] Added Files saved before this version open with Live Bump matching how their partings were saved. If some had bump and some did not, it opens on. [panel: appearance] Added Freeze and Apply now warn you in their confirm box when the last bake had no Normal map. [panel: bake] Changed Normal cannot be ticked in the Bake block while Live Bump is off, since there would be no bump to bake. [panel: bake] Fixed Partings turning magenta once a head carried about 25 of them in Material Preview on some graphics cards. Every parting's warp now shares one image, so the count no longer runs into the limit. Run Repair Partings once to move partings already in a file over. [panel: header] Fixed New partings tilting into the head on the crown, sides and back. The facing rotation was being worked out in reverse, and the surface weld drifted off the surface on non-square partings. [panel: placement-keys] Changed New partings stick to the surface by position only, and the tool sets their facing rotation itself. They face straight out from the surface wherever they are placed, whatever their proportions. [panel: placement-keys] Changed Moving a new parting with G turns it to face the surface at its new spot as you drag. Any twist you added with R stays. [panel: placement-keys] Changed Duplicate gives the copy the same surface weld as its source, so a copy sits exactly the way its original does. [panel: parting-list] Changed Partings already placed are not changed. Files from earlier versions keep their old weld, and Repair Partings leaves it alone, so anything you have placed stays put. [panel: placement-keys] Changed Linked mirrors still follow their source. Once unlinked, a mirror turns to face the surface the next time you move it. [panel: parting-list] Fixed The key guide shown while placing partings now appears only in the viewport you started from. With a second 3D viewport open it was drawn in both, and cut off in the smaller one. [panel: placement-keys] Fixed The head's own material is now kept when you save. Once a head had partings nothing else used it, so saving dropped it. Sync From Original, New Style, Delete Style and Reset Partings could then no longer find it. [panel: header] Added Parting Mask viewer. A thumbnail shows the mask new partings will use. Click it to pick from your masks. With no mask chosen, a line underneath says which image will be used. [panel: target] Added + adds a mask from an image file. It is saved inside the .blend, so the file keeps working if the image moves. [panel: target] Added Arrows beside the viewer step through your masks. [panel: target] Added The bin takes the shown mask out of your mask list. Partings already using it keep it. [panel: target] Added Replace puts the shown mask on the ticked partings, or on the highlighted one when nothing is ticked. Position, shape and settings stay as they were, and linked mirrors follow. The button names what it will change. If Preview Mode is on it turns off so the new mask shows. [panel: target] Changed The mask list shows only masks: images added with +, and images your partings already use. Baked maps and other textures in the file no longer appear in it. [panel: target] Changed Add Parting is now Place Parting, with a target icon. It is larger and has space around it. [panel: placement-keys] Changed Style and Parting Mask each sit in their own box. [panel: target] Added Edit Warp, in Parting Parameters. Drag the handles in the viewport to warp a parting. Enter confirms, and Esc or right-click puts the warp back as it was. The button stays pressed while that parting is being edited, and pressing it again also confirms. [panel: parting-parameters] Added Lattice warps. Convert to Lattice turns a parting's corner warp into a 2 x 2 lattice without changing how it looks. P- and P+, Q- and Q+ change the rows and columns, from 2 to 8 each way. docs.text: Glossary ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Short definitions of the words this guide and the panel use. Parting ¶ One parting image placed on the head. Each one is an Empty plus a shading effect in the head's material. See How A Parting Is Built . Stamp ¶ The panel's word for one parting, as in Stamps: 2 in the key guide or Live · 2 stamp(s) . It means the same as parting. Empty ¶ A Blender object with no mesh. Each parting has one, and it sets where the parting sits and which way it faces. Moving the Empty moves the parting. Pending Mirror ¶ A mirrored copy of a parting that you haven't kept yet. Confirm it to keep it as a parting of its own, or deactivate it to remove it. See Mirror Partings . Preview Proxy ¶ The low-resolution stand-in that Preview Mode shows in place of your live partings. The status line calls it cached, as in Preview · 2 stamps cached at 1024px . See Preview . Frozen Layer ¶ A set of partings baked into a checkpoint by Freeze Layer and taken out of the material. Frozen work stays in your maps. You can have 3 per material. Coverage Map ¶ The README's name for the Alpha map. It shows where your partings are, not what colour they are. Style ¶ A complete set of partings on one head. One style shows at a time, and the rest are parked. See Styles . Partings Material ¶ The copy of your head's material that the add-on works on. Its name ends in _Partings , for example Material.001_Partings . Your original material stays in the file. Live Bump ¶ The switch at the bottom of the Appearance box that shows parting relief in the viewport. It starts off. Turn it on before you bake a Normal map. See Live Bump . Parting Mask ¶ The image each new parting is stamped with. Pick it in the Parting Mask box. See Parting Mask . Edit Warp ¶ A way to bend a parting by dragging handles in the viewport. See Edit Warp . Lattice ¶ A warp with a grid of handles, from 2 x 2 up to 8 x 8. A corner warp has 4 handles. See Convert To Lattice . Soft Radius ¶ How far a drag in Edit Warp pulls nearby handles along. At 0 only the handle you hold moves. See Soft Radius . Fold Guard ¶ Stops a lattice warp from folding back through itself. See Fold Guard . Names You See In The Outliner ¶ The add-on adds a few things to your scene. You can leave them alone. Name What it is PARTING_Empty_000 , PARTING_Empty_001 … One Empty per parting Partings.head The collection holding the Empties, named after your head head - Style 1 Where a parked style's Empties are kept PARTING_Mirror_Root.head A helper for mirroring, named after your head Recommended next: Changelog

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Find your symptom below. Each entry gives the fix first, then the reason. I Cannot See Any Partings ¶ Switch the viewport to Material Preview or Rendered shading. Press Z to pick one. Partings are shading, so they don't show in Solid . Already in Material Preview? Check these: The parting isn't hidden. Each one has an eye in the Parting List . The panel is working on the right head. See Target . The parting isn't on the far side of the head. Orbit round before you assume it failed. You switched styles with Preview on. See Style . A Parting Looks Doubled Or Folded ¶ Update to V1.3.1, run Repair Partings once, then look at the parting again. A parting with strongly moved corners could show a faint second copy of itself, folded back over the first. Partings already in a file keep their old look until you run Repair once. Partings Look Flat, Or The Bump Sliders Have Gone ¶ Turn on Live Bump . The switch is at the bottom of the Appearance box. See Live Bump . From V2.0.0 it starts off. Bump is the slowest part of the material for Blender to rebuild, so placing stays quick without it. Bump Strength and Bump Distance show again while it is on. The switch covers every partings material in the file, including parked styles and other heads. Partings Turn Magenta In Material Preview ¶ Update to V2.0.0, run Repair Partings once, then look again. On some graphics cards, a head carrying about 25 partings could turn them magenta. Every parting's warp now shares one image, so the count no longer runs into the limit. Repair moves partings already in a file over. Its message counts the warp tile node(s) added . Place Parting Does Nothing ¶ Select your head mesh, or set it as Target . Make sure the head has a material. Then move the mouse over the head. The preview only follows the cursor while it is over the head. If the add-on can't start, the status bar says why. See Place Parting for each message. Bake Partings Is Greyed Out Or Refuses ¶ Check these, in order: Preview is on. Select Disable Preview first. The head has no UV map. Unwrap the head first. The head has no partings. Place at least one. Only Normal is ticked and Live Bump is off. Turn on Live Bump , or tick another map too. Pending mirrors don't block Bake Partings . A dialog asks whether to include them. See Include pending mirrors in bake . My Bake Has No Normal Map ¶ Turn on Live Bump , then bake again. With Live Bump off there is no bump to bake. The Normal tick box is greyed out, and the bake skips it. If Normal was the only map ticked, the bake stops with a warning. Freeze Layer and Apply Bake warn you in their confirm box when the last bake had no Normal map. See Apply Bake . The Face Shows Through My Baked Normal Map ¶ Update to V1.3.0 or later, run Repair Partings once, then bake again. Older versions let the bump reach outside the partings. Eyes, nose, lips and ears showed up in the normal map. Until you run Repair, the file looks unchanged. That is expected. Partings Bake With Small Holes In Them ¶ Raise Samples in the Bake box. The default of 16 leaves around 0.4% of the parting area holed. Past 16 the gains fall off sharply while the bake gets slower. Dark Speckles Or Short Dashes Inside My Partings After Baking ¶ Update to V1.1.0 or later, then bake again. The dashes only show in the baked maps and the transparent export, never in the viewport. Maps baked with an older version keep them until you re-bake. Baking Takes Much Longer Than It Used To ¶ This is expected from V1.1.0. The old speed came at the cost of dropped pixels in every map. To work faster, bake at a lower Resolution while you work, and raise it for the final pass. Keep Normal Resolution high, since it carries the fine detail. The Baked Colour Is Darker Than My Hair Color Swatch ¶ Lower Detail . At 0 the bake matches your swatch. Detail darkens the parting, and the bake shows your colour after Detail is applied. The hue stays the same. Only the brightness changes. Partings I Froze Have Disappeared From My Maps ¶ Update to V1.1.0 or later. From then on, frozen partings survive any number of later bakes. Before V1.1.0, freezing then baking more than once lost frozen partings from the Alpha map. The Color, Normal and Roughness maps were never affected. Alpha already lost can't be recovered. Re-place and re-bake those partings, or carry on and let your next freeze start fresh. Freeze Layer Is Greyed Out ¶ Check these, in order: You haven't baked yet. Select Bake Partings first. Freeze Layer reuses that bake. Mirrors are pending. Confirm or deactivate them. You've used all 3 freezes on this material. The limit can't be raised. Start a new style instead. My Baked Maps Vanished ¶ The usual cause is File > Clean Up > Purge Unused Data . Bake again to get them back. Some maps are kept on the material without being plugged into anything. Blender thinks they are unused and deletes them. The Alpha map, the transparent-export pass and every frozen snapshot are in that group. A lost frozen snapshot can't be re-baked, because its partings are gone from your scene. Before you purge, open the Image Editor and switch on the shield icon (fake user) for those maps. Saving your file is safe, because the maps are packed into it. Partings Are Doubled, Or Land In The Wrong Place, On A Mirrored Mesh ¶ If your head has a Mirror modifier, don't also mirror partings with the add-on. You would be mirroring twice. Place partings on the real half only, and turn the Mirror modifier off for renders. See Work On A Head With A Mirror Modifier . The Viewport Is Slow ¶ Select Enable Preview . Nothing is committed, and Disable Preview brings full shading back. Then close the Shader Editor if it is open. For partings that are settled, bake and use Freeze Layer . See Keep The Viewport Fast . Preview Mode Is Still On After I Finish Placing ¶ This is on purpose. The partings you just placed stay live on top of the stand-in, so they are still quick to adjust. Select Disable Preview when you want full shading back. Preview Mode is saved with the file. A file saved with it on opens with it on. Dashed Lines Run From Every Parting To The Head ¶ Select the Relationship Lines icon in the panel header. It hides the lines in that viewport and changes nothing in your file. The Transparent Export Has A Pale Or Skin-Coloured Edge ¶ Bake once more with V1.1.0 or later, then export again. The export now takes its colour from a pass that leaves the skin out. A soft edge keeps the parting's own colour. A material last baked with an older version falls back to the old look. The status bar message after saving tells you which was used. 16-bit Export Looks The Same And The File Is Much Bigger ¶ Switch back to 8-bit unless you see banding in the colour of a soft edge. 16-bit helps the colour, not the transparency. Transparency is stored at 8-bit either way, in a file about three times the size. If the banding is in the edge's transparency, 16-bit won't help. Save Transparent Is Unavailable ¶ Tick Alpha in the Bake box and bake again. Save Transparent needs both Color and Alpha baked, and Alpha is off by default. The Key Guide Has Disappeared From The Viewport ¶ Look along the top of the viewport. If the guide can't be drawn, it shows there as a single line for the rest of the session. To get the full guide back, turn the add-on off and on again in Edit > Preferences > Add-ons . This doesn't touch your partings, styles or baked maps. If it keeps happening, email the console text to help@ebonix.com. On Windows, open it with Window > Toggle System Console . On macOS and Linux, start Blender from a terminal. Ctrl+Z Crashed Blender After I Placed Partings ¶ Update to V1.3.0 or later. Now, one Ctrl+Z after you finish undoes the whole session. Ctrl+Z while placing still removes one parting at a time. I Cannot See The Mirror Toggle In The Sidebar ¶ It was removed in V1.2.0. Press M while placing to turn mirroring on and off. Partings you already mirrored are unaffected. The Depth Slider Has Gone ¶ It was removed in V1.2.0 and is fixed at 0.5. Partings placed earlier keep the value they had. An Appearance Slider Will Not Go As High As It Used To ¶ Each parting's sliders now stop at the same limits as the shared ones. Opacity stops at 100. If a parting was set past a limit, Repair Partings brings it back to that limit. Check anything you pushed far on purpose before you run Repair. Still Stuck ¶ Email help@ebonix.com with: your Blender version the add-on version, from Edit > Preferences > Add-ons what you did, what you expected, and what happened a screenshot of the panel and of the problem If the problem is in a baked map or an export, attach the image itself. docs.text: Shape A Parting With Edit Warp ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Bend a parting so it follows the head, for example along a hairline, by dragging handles in the viewport. You Need First Place Partings The Parting Parameters box. It shows while a parting is picked. See Parting Parameters . Your browser cannot play this clip. Read the steps as text . Bending a parting's corners, then turning it into a lattice for more handles Read the steps as text Bend The Corners ¶ In the parting list, select the parting you want to shape. In Parting Parameters , select Edit Warp . Four handles appear on the parting. Drag a handle with the left mouse button. Press Enter to keep the shape. To cancel instead, press Esc or right-click. The parting goes back to how it was before you selected Edit Warp . The middle mouse button still orbits the view while you edit. A key guide in the viewport lists the keys. Add More Handles With A Lattice ¶ Four handles can't follow every curve. A lattice gives the parting a grid of handles instead. Check Edit Warp is not pressed. If it is, press Enter first. Select Convert To Lattice . The parting keeps its shape and gets a 2 x 2 lattice. Select P+ to add a column of handles. Select Q+ to add a row. The size shows underneath, for example Lattice 4 x 4 . Select Edit Warp . Drag the handles to the shape you want. Press Enter to keep the shape. Your browser cannot play this clip. Read the steps as text . Shaping a 4 x 4 lattice along the hairline Read the steps as text Set the number of rows and columns before you start shaping. Changing the size later can shift the shape. Each side goes up to 8 handles. Control How Far A Drag Spreads ¶ While you hold a handle, scroll to change Soft Radius . It sets how far a drag pulls the nearby handles along. At 0 only the handle you hold moves. On a lattice, Fold Guard stops the warp folding back through itself. Hold Shift and scroll to change it. To go back to a plain corner warp, select Reset To Corners . The lattice shape is not kept. If You're Stuck Convert To Lattice or P+ is greyed out? Press Enter to finish the edit first. A parting looks doubled or folded? See A Parting Looks Doubled Or Folded . Every control in detail: Edit Warp . Recommended next: Make Every Parting Match

docs.text: Make Every Parting Match ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Give every parting on a head the same colour and look. There are two ways, and they suit different jobs. Keep Them Linked ¶ Use this when you want one set of values to drive every parting from now on. Select the link icon in the Appearance heading. Check the heading now reads Global Appearance . Change the sliders. Every parting follows. [3] Linked: every parting takes the same colour When you turn linking on, the first parting in the list sets the starting values. docs.text: Appearance ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 These sliders set how a parting looks. Each parting has its own set, unless you link them. [1] The Appearance box with Link Appearance on The box sits under the parting list, once the head has at least one parting. Its heading tells you what you are editing: Heading Means Global Appearance Link Appearance is on. One set of values drives every parting. Appearance · Parting 002 Link Appearance is off. You are editing the parting named after the dot. Appearance Link Appearance is off and no parting is picked. The box says "Select a parting to edit its appearance". Link Appearance ¶ The link icon at the right of the heading. It is off by default. Its tooltip reads: Share appearance settings across all partings. Turn it on to give every parting the same look. The values of the first parting in the list become the shared set. With it off, each parting keeps its own values. Copy Settings To All is then available on each parting. See Copy Settings To All . Turn it off again and each parting keeps the shared values until you change them. Turning it back on overwrites every parting with the first parting's values. Hair Color ¶ The colour of the parting. The default is a near black. A baked colour can come out darker than this swatch, because Detail darkens it. See Detail . Opacity ¶ Default 50 , from 0 to 100. How solid the parting is. At 0 it disappears. Raising it fills the parting in, though above about 25 the change is small. Opacity and Divide work together. See Divide . Divide ¶ Default 0.5 , from 0 to 2 on the slider. Divides Opacity . Raise it to thin the parting out, or lower it to fill it in. At 0 the parting disappears. For example, Opacity 50 with Divide 1 looks the same as Opacity 25 with Divide 0.5. Hair Roughness ¶ Default 0.5 , from 0 to 1. How matte the parting is. 0 is glossy and 1 is fully matte. It shows in the baked Roughness map, and in the viewport wherever your material reflects light. Rough Variation ¶ Default 0.5 , from -1 to 4 on the slider. Shifts the roughness across the parting. Higher values make the parting glossier overall. It shows in the baked Roughness map. Detail ¶ Default 1 , from 0 to 2 on the slider. Detail darkens the parting. At 0 the bake matches your Hair Color swatch. Higher values make it darker. At 2 it is much darker. Lower Detail if you want the bake closer to the swatch. Live Bump ¶ The switch at the bottom of the box. It reads Live Bump: Off or Live Bump: On , and it is off by default. Its tooltip reads: Show parting relief in the viewport. Slower to compile: turn off while placing partings, and on before baking a Normal map. Bump is the slowest part of the material for Blender to rebuild, so leave it off while you place partings. Turn it on before you bake, or the Normal map has no bump in it. See Color / Normal / Roughness / Alpha . The line under the switch tells you which way to set it. While it is off, it reads Turn on when baking partings . While it is on, it reads Turn off whilst placing partings . Bump Strength and Bump Distance show under the switch only while it is on. The switch covers every partings material in the file, including parked styles and other heads. It shows even when no parting is picked. Bump Strength ¶ Shown while Live Bump is on. Default 1.07 , from 0 to 5 on the slider. How strongly the hair texture stands out. At 0 the parting looks flatter and lighter. Higher values make it darker and more textured. Bump Distance ¶ Shown while Live Bump is on. Default -0.04 , from -1 to 20 on the slider. Fine-tunes the bump. Small changes do little. At 20 the parting is a little darker than at the default. Where Did Depth Go? Depth was removed from the panel in V1.2.0 and is fixed at 0.5. Partings placed before then keep the value they had. See The Depth Slider Has Gone . If You're Stuck A slider stops lower than it used to? See An Appearance Slider Will Not Go As High As It Used To . The bake is darker than your colour? See The Baked Colour Is Darker Than My Hair Color Swatch . Anything else: Still Stuck . Recommended next: Parting Parameters

docs.text: Bake ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Bake Partings renders your partings into image maps you can save and use elsewhere. Your partings stay live afterwards, so you can keep tweaking and bake again. The box starts collapsed. Select the arrow beside Bake to open it. [1] The Bake box, open, before a bake, with Live Bump on The settings are greyed out until the head has a parting and a UV map. Mirror Modifier Warning ¶ This red warning appears at the top if the head has a Mirror modifier switched on for rendering. It reads: Mirror modifier — partings on the mirrored half share UVs and will be lost in the bake . See Work On A Head With A Mirror Modifier for what to do. Resolution ¶ The size of the Color, Roughness and Alpha maps, in pixels: 512 , 1024 , 2048 or 4096 . The default is 2048 . Normal Resolution ¶ The size of the Normal map, set apart from the others. The Normal map carries the fine bump detail, so it benefits from more pixels. Options run from 512 to 8192 . The default is 4096 . Normal Filtering ¶ Shown while Normal is ticked. Linear or Cubic , applied to the normal pass only. Leave it on Linear . The README says Cubic makes the blockiness slightly worse. Margin Type ¶ How the margin is filled. Extend repeats the border pixels, which is what the tool has always done. Adjacent Faces samples across UV seams instead. The default is Extend . Samples ¶ How finely the bake is sampled. The default is 16 . Raise it if your partings bake with small holes. Past 16 the gains fall off sharply while the bake keeps getting slower. The README calls it Bake Samples . Margin ¶ How far the bake spreads past the edge of each UV island, in pixels, so seams don't show. The default is 32 , from 0 to 64. It also spreads the bump outside each parting by the same amount. Lower it to narrow that spread. Color / Normal / Roughness / Alpha ¶ Tick the maps you want. Color , Normal and Roughness are on by default. Alpha is off. Alpha makes a coverage map: where your partings are, not what colour they are. You only need it for Save Transparent . With Color and Alpha both ticked, the bake takes two extra passes rather than one. Normal only bakes while Live Bump is on. Live Bump starts off, so a first bake skips Normal unless you turn it on. While Live Bump is off, the Normal tick box is greyed out and the bake skips it. If Normal is the only map ticked, the bake stops with Normal skipped: Live Bump is off. Turn it on to bake a Normal map. Bake Partings ¶ Renders the ticked maps. Baking again is safe: the new maps carry the old ones forward, even if you change the resolution. It is greyed out while Preview is on. Select Disable Preview first. See Preview . Once a bake exists, the save options appear underneath. See Saving Textures . Include pending mirrors in bake ¶ Select Bake Partings with mirrors still pending, and a dialog says how many. It offers this tick box. It is on by default, so pending mirrors bake along with your other partings. Untick it to bake only the partings you have kept. Apply Bake ¶ Swaps the live partings for the baked images and deletes their Empties. This is the step that makes the hair ready for export. Press Ctrl+Z to undo it. It is greyed out until you have baked, and while any mirrors are pending. Blender asks you to confirm first. The status bar then says how many maps it applied and how many Empties it removed. If your last bake had no Normal map, the confirm box warns you first. It reads Last bake had no Normal map: parting relief will be lost. An older Normal map may still be there. Then it reads Last bake skipped Normal: an older Normal map will be used. Freeze Layer ¶ Takes your last bake as a checkpoint and clears the partings so far, so you can keep placing on top. Frozen work stays in your maps however many times you bake afterwards. Use it when a set of partings is settled. Select Bake Partings first. Freeze Layer reuses that bake and does not bake on its own. You can freeze 3 times per material. When you place more partings after a freeze, the button counts your freezes, for example Freeze Layer (1/3) . It is greyed out while any mirrors are pending. After a freeze, the frozen partings show on the head as part of the baked image. Their Empties are gone. The list starts empty again. Its confirm box carries the same Normal map warning as Apply Bake . Mesh has no UV map ¶ Shown at the bottom of the box when the head has no UV map. Baking needs one. Add a UV map to the head, then come back. If You're Stuck Bake Partings is greyed out? See Bake Partings Is Greyed Out Or Refuses . Small holes or dark speckles in the maps? See Partings Bake With Small Holes In Them . Freeze Layer is greyed out? See Freeze Layer Is Greyed Out . Recommended next: Saving Textures

docs.text: Panel Header ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Four small icons sit at the right end of the Parting Placer Tool panel title. This page covers each one, left to right. [1] The four header icons, left to right: Sync From Original, Relationship Lines, Repair Partings, Reset Partings Sync From Original ¶ The link icon, first from the left. It is on by default. The icon shows a closed link when on and a broken link when off. Its tooltip reads: Match the partings material to the head's original. While it is on, edits you make to the head's original material carry across to the partings material. Switch it off to keep the two apart. Relationship Lines ¶ The second icon. It switches off the dashed lines Blender draws from every parting's Empty to the head. It changes nothing in your file. It applies only to the 3D view the panel is in. It has no effect while Overlays are switched off. Repair Partings ¶ The refresh arrow, third from the left. Repair rebuilds the links between partings, Empties and the material if something has come adrift. It also brings older files up to date, including the limits on the appearance sliders. Run it once in each existing file after you update the add-on. In V2 it also moves each parting's warp onto a shared warp image. That stops partings turning magenta once a head carries about 25 of them. Its message then counts the warp tile node(s) added . Check Pushed Sliders First If a parting's appearance slider sits past its current limit, Repair brings it back to that limit. Check anything you pushed far on purpose before you run it. Repair and Reset are greyed out until the panel has a head. Set a Target , or select a mesh. Reset Partings ¶ The trash can, last on the right. Reset removes every parting from the object and puts the material back to its original state. To clear the partings and keep the material you tuned, use Delete All in the parting list instead. See Delete All . If You're Stuck A parting looks doubled? See A Parting Looks Doubled Or Folded . The face shows in your normal map? See The Face Shows Through My Baked Normal Map . docs.text: Parting List ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Every parting you place shows up in this list. From here you pick, hide, copy, mirror, reorder and remove them. [1] The parting list with two partings, one ticked Applied Partings ¶ The heading counts your partings, for example Applied Partings (2) . New partings are named Parting 001 , Parting 002 and so on. Pending Mirrors ¶ A mirror starts out pending, so you can see it before you keep it. While any are pending, a line under the heading counts them, for example Pending Mirrors: 2 . With more than five pending, a warning appears: Confirm or deactivate pending mirrors . Confirm All ¶ Keeps every pending mirror as a parting of its own. The button shows how many, for example Confirm All (2) . The README calls it Confirm All Pending . Deactivate All ¶ Throws away every pending mirror. The README calls it Deactivate All Pending . Blender asks you to confirm first. Tick Box ¶ Tick the box beside a parting's name to pick it for the ticked-row buttons. Tick as many as you like, in any order. Shift -click a second box to tick every row between the two. Eye (One Parting) ¶ The eye at the end of a row hides that parting, or shows it again. Hiding a parting also hides its pending mirror, if it has one. A hidden parting stays hidden when you switch styles and back. See Style . Search And Sort Row ¶ The row under the list is always open. Type in Search to show only partings whose name contains your text. The sort buttons switch between your stack order and A to Z, and flip the order. Select ¶ The arrow beside the list selects the active parting's Empty in the viewport, so you can move it. Duplicate ¶ Makes a copy of the active parting, along with its own Empty. The copy carries the whole warp, lattice included, and sits on the head the same way as its source. Mirror ¶ Makes a pending mirror of the active parting on the other side of the head. The status bar says Pending mirror created. While the parting has a pending mirror, the button stays pressed in. Select it again to choose Confirm (make permanent) or Deactivate (destroy mirror) . For the full workflow, see Mirror Partings . Mirrors carry the whole warp. A linked mirror follows lattice edits on its source while you drag. See Edit Warp . Up And Down ¶ Moves the active parting up or down the stack. Up is greyed out on the top row, and Down on the bottom row. Moving A Parting Into The Top Row A move that puts a different parting in the top row strips the head's skin texture. The head turns a flat tan. Press Ctrl+Z straight away to bring it back. Repair Partings does not fix it. Where two partings overlap, the one lower in the list is drawn on top. Moving a parting changes which one shows. X (Remove) ¶ Removes the active parting and its Empty. Trash (Delete All) ¶ The trash can under X removes every parting on the head. It keeps the material you have been tuning, so the next parting you place carries your settings over. The status bar reports what went, ending with Material kept. To put the head's plain skin material back as well, use Reset Partings instead. Blender asks first, for example Delete all 3 parting(s)? with Delete All and Cancel . Fix Duplicate Names ¶ If two partings end up with the same name, a red button appears, for example Fix 2 Duplicate Name(s) . Select it to give each one its own name. Eye (Ticked Row) ¶ Once you tick a parting, a row appears above Show All / Hide All . It starts with a count, for example 2 ticked . Its eye hides the ticked partings, or shows them again. If some are hidden and some showing, it hides all of them. The icon always shows what the next press will do. Delete ¶ Removes every ticked parting. Select ¶ Selects the ticked partings' Empties in the viewport, so you can move them together. Hidden partings are skipped, and the status bar says how many. Clear ¶ Unticks everything. Show All / Hide All ¶ Shows or hides every parting on the head at once. If You're Stuck A parting has gone missing? See I Cannot See Any Partings . Can't find the mirror button? See I Cannot See The Mirror Toggle In The Sidebar . Anything else: Still Stuck . Recommended next: Appearance

docs.text: Parting Parameters ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 This box holds the settings for the one parting picked in the list. It only appears while a parting is picked, and its second line names that parting. [1] Parting Parameters with corner markers shown Rotation ¶ Turns the parting on the head. The default is 0 . The value is in radians, not degrees. A quarter turn is 1.571 , and a half turn is 3.142 . Scale X / Scale Y ¶ Fine-tune the parting's size along each side. Higher values make it smaller . Lower values make it bigger. The template default is 5 , but a placed parting can show other values. Corner BL / BR / TL / TR ¶ Four rows, one per corner of the parting, each with an X and a Y field. All start at 0, 0 . Turn on Show Corner Markers to see which corner of the parting each row belongs to. Changing a corner's X or Y pulls that corner of the parting out of square. Use it to bend a parting's shape to fit the head. On a lattice parting the four rows stay in the box, but the lattice sets the shape. See Convert To Lattice . Show Corner Markers ¶ Shows a label at each corner of the picked parting, so you can tell which way round it is. The button then reads Hide Corner Markers . The markers are display only. Nothing is added to your scene and nothing is rendered. Inset ¶ Shown while corner markers are on. It sets how far out the labels sit, as a fraction of the way to each corner. At 1.0 they sit on the corners themselves. The default is 0.7 , from 0 to 1.5. The README calls it Marker Inset . Lift ¶ Shown while corner markers are on. It raises the labels off the surface so they read clear of the parting. The default is 0.6 . The README calls it Marker Lift . Size ¶ Shown while corner markers are on. It sets the text size of the labels. The default is 13 , from 6 upwards. Its tooltip says it follows the Resolution Scale in your Blender preferences. The labels stay in step with the rest of the interface. Edit Warp ¶ Bends the picked parting by dragging handles in the viewport. A corner warp has 4 handles. A lattice has one handle for each lattice point. Select Edit Warp , then drag a handle with the left mouse button. The middle mouse button still orbits the view. Press Enter to keep the result. Esc or right-click puts the warp back as it was. Selecting Edit Warp again also keeps the result. The button stays pressed while that parting is being edited. While you hold a handle, scroll changes Soft Radius . Shift and scroll changes Fold Guard . A key guide in the viewport lists these keys while you edit. The sidebar stays usable during an edit. Its tooltip reads: Drag the handles in the viewport to warp this parting. Mirror and Duplicate carry the whole warp. A linked mirror follows lattice edits on its source while you drag. For a walkthrough, see Shape A Parting With Edit Warp . Convert To Lattice ¶ Shown on a parting with a corner warp. It turns the corner warp into a 2 x 2 lattice without changing how the parting looks. It is greyed out while that parting's warp is being edited. Lattice Size ¶ Shown on a lattice parting. P- and P+ take a column of handles away or add one. Q- and Q+ do the same for rows. Each side goes from 2 to 8, so a lattice has up to 64 handles. The row underneath shows the size, for example Lattice 3 x 4 . Changing the size resamples the warp to fit the new grid, so its shape can shift. It shifts more when you take a row or column away. Its tooltip reads: Add or remove a lattice row or column. The current warp is resampled to fit the new grid, so its shape can shift, more so when removing one. These buttons are greyed out while that parting's warp is being edited. Reset To Corners ¶ Shown on a lattice parting, beside the size. It puts the parting back to a corner warp. The corner warp comes from the four Corner rows, so the lattice shape is not kept. It is greyed out while that parting's warp is being edited. Soft Radius ¶ Shown on a lattice parting. Default 0.5 , from 0 to 2. How far a drag pulls nearby handles along with the one you hold, as a share of the lattice size. At 0 only that handle moves. A change applies from the next handle you grab. Scroll changes it on a corner warp too, where the slider is hidden. Its tooltip reads: Soft-radius falloff for Edit Warp dragging, as a fraction of the lattice size. 0 drags a single control point. Fold Guard ¶ Shown on a lattice parting. docs.text: Turns the parting on the head. The default is 0 . The value is in radians, not degrees. A quarter turn is 1.571 , and a half turn is 3.142 .

docs.text: Place Parting And Placement Keys ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Place Parting puts you into placing mode on the head. This page covers the button and every key you can use until you finish. [1] The key guide while placing, with size mode on Place Parting ¶ Select Place Parting in the panel, then move the mouse over the head. A preview parting follows the cursor while it is over the head. The first parting on a head starts at a size worked out from the head's own size. After that, each session starts at the size of your last parting. Rotation goes back to 0°, and mirror starts off. A new parting faces straight out from the surface wherever you place it, whatever its proportions. Move it later with G and it keeps facing the surface as you drag. Any twist you added with R stays. Partings placed with an earlier version are left as they were. If the head already has partings and Auto Preview is ticked, Preview switches on as you start. See Auto Preview . If Place Parting refuses to start, the status bar says why: Message What to do Run this from a 3D Viewport. Start it from the 3D viewport's sidebar. No target mesh. Pick one in the Partings panel or select a mesh object. Set Target , or select the head. See Target . Head has no material to stamp into. Give the head a material first. Material slot is empty. Put a material in the head's empty material slot. Add > Mesh Menu Entries ¶ The 3D viewport's Add > Mesh menu has three entries at the bottom: Place Partings , Repair Partings and Reset Partings . Place Partings does the same as Place Parting . The other two match the Repair Partings and Reset Partings icons in the panel header. Key Guide ¶ While you place, a key guide sits in the viewport. Its title is PLACING PARTINGS , with Stamps under it counting the partings placed this session. Each row shows a key, what it does, and its current state: Row Shows LMB Stamp S Size Two numbers, one per side of the parting. [SIZE] appears while size mode is on. X / Y Axis Lock [X] , [Y] or [R] for what the scroll wheel is locked to, or [-] for nothing R + Scroll Rotate The angle in degrees M Mirror [ON] or [OFF] Ctrl + Z Undo RMB / Esc Done The guide goes away when you finish. It only shows in the viewport you started placing from. Mouse Move ¶ The preview parting follows the cursor while it is over the head. Over empty space, nothing appears. S ¶ Press S to switch to size mode. The key guide shows [SIZE] , and each scroll notch makes the parting a little bigger or smaller on both sides. Press S again to leave size mode. Scrolling then zooms the viewport as usual. The size you end on carries to every parting you place afterwards, including in later sessions. X / Y ¶ Press X or Y to lock resizing to one side of the parting. X changes the first size number and Y the second. Size mode stays on. Press the same key again to release the lock. R + Scroll ¶ Press R , then scroll to rotate the parting by 5° per notch. Pressing R turns size mode off. Press R again to release it. Scrolling then zooms the viewport again. Ctrl + Scroll ¶ Hold Ctrl and scroll to resize both sides without pressing S first. This shortcut is not listed in the key guide. M ¶ Press M to turn mirroring on. The key guide shows [ON] and a mirrored preview appears on the other side. Press M again to turn it off. Every session starts with mirroring off. For what happens to a mirror after you place it, see Mirror Partings . Left Click ¶ Click to place the parting where the preview sits. Placing mode stays on, so you can keep clicking to add more. Ctrl+Z ¶ While you place, Ctrl+Z removes the last parting. Press it again to remove the one before. After you finish, one Ctrl+Z takes back the whole session. Right Click / Esc ¶ Right-click or press Esc to finish. The status bar reports how many partings you placed in that session. For example: Finished — 2 parting decal(s) on 'Material.001_Partings'. If Preview came on as you started, the message adds that Preview Mode is still on. See Preview Mode Is Still On After I Finish Placing . If You're Stuck Nothing follows the mouse? See Place Parting Does Nothing . The key guide is missing? See The Key Guide Has Disappeared From The Viewport . Placed a parting and can't see it? See I Cannot See Any Partings . Recommended next: Preview

docs.text: Preview ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Preview Mode bakes a low-resolution stand-in for your partings and shows that in the viewport. Blender stops redrawing every parting live, so the viewport stays quick. This box appears once the head has at least one parting. [1] The Preview box with Preview Mode on Enable Preview / Disable Preview ¶ Select Enable Preview to bake the stand-in. It takes a few seconds. When it's done, the status bar confirms it. For example: Preview Mode — 2 stamps cached at 1024px. The button then reads Disable Preview . Select Disable Preview to get full shading back. Nothing is committed and nothing is lost. A parting you hid stays hidden. While Preview is on: Partings you place stay live on top of the stand-in, so they are still quick to adjust. Bake Partings refuses to run. Turn Preview off first. See Bake Partings . Switching styles can hide partings by mistake. Turn Preview off first. See Style . Replace in the Parting Mask box turns Preview off, so the new mask shows. Preview Mode is saved with the file. A file saved with it on opens with it on. The button is greyed out if the head has no UV map. Auto Preview ¶ Ticked by default. Its tooltip reads: Freeze existing partings to a proxy while placing (above 30, live partings may fail to compile) . With it ticked, starting Place Parting on a head that already has partings switches Preview on first. Only the partings you place in that session are live. Preview stays on after you finish. If you untick it and the head has more than 30 partings, the box shows a warning with your count. For example: 31 partings — placing without Auto Preview may fail to compile . Preview Res ¶ The resolution of the stand-in. The default is 512 px . Option Tooltip 256 px Fast, lower quality 512 px Balanced (default) 1024 px Higher quality, slower bake It is hidden while Preview is on, so pick it before you select Enable Preview . Status Lines ¶ The last line of the box tells you what the viewport is showing: Line Means Live · 2 stamp(s) Preview is off. Every parting is drawn live. Preview · 2 stamps cached at 1024px Preview is on, at that resolution. Live · 50 stamps — Preview Mode recommended Preview is off and the head has 50 or more partings. The counts include partings you have hidden. If You're Stuck Preview is still on after you finished placing? See Preview Mode Is Still On After I Finish Placing . The viewport is slow? docs.text: Saving Textures ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 Once you have baked, this row appears at the bottom of the Bake box. It writes your maps out of Blender as PNG files. [1] The save row after a bake with Alpha ticked Baked: Line ¶ Lists the maps you have baked, for example Baked: Color, Normal, Roughness . Bit Depth ¶ The unlabelled dropdown: 8-bit or 16-bit . It applies to Save Transparent . The default is 8-bit , which is right for almost everything. 16-bit gives the colour more levels to work with, but not the transparency. A 16-bit file has the same 256 steps of transparency as an 8-bit one. It is also about three times the size. Use it only when you see banding in the colour of a soft edge. Premultiplied ¶ Multiplies the colour by the transparency before writing Save Transparent 's file. It is off by default. Leave it off unless your game engine asks for premultiplied alpha. Off keeps colour in the fully transparent areas, so nothing bleeds through when the engine shrinks the texture. The README calls it Premultiplied Alpha . Save Textures ¶ Pick a folder, and every baked map is saved there as its own PNG. The file names include the head, the style, the map and its size. For example: head_Style 1_Partings_Color_1024.png . The status bar confirms how many it saved. Save Transparent ¶ Writes one PNG with your parting colour and its transparency together. It is ready to layer over a scalp texture in a game engine. It uses this head's UV layout, so the file only fits this head. It needs both Color and Alpha baked. Until then it is greyed out and the row says "Tick Alpha and re-bake for transparent". The README calls it Save Textures (Transparent) . The status bar message says where the colour came from. If it says re-bake to use the premultiplied map , your last bake came from an older version. Bake once more, then save again. The file is named after the head, for example head_Partings_Transparent.png . The status bar confirms the bit depth and alpha type it used. If You're Stuck Save Transparent is greyed out? See Save Transparent Is Unavailable . The transparent file has a pale edge? docs.text: Target And Styles ¶ Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 This page covers the top of the panel. Target picks the head you are working on. Under it, the Style box holds that head's styles, and the Parting Mask box sets the image new partings use. The large Place Parting button sits below them. See Place Parting . [1] The top of the panel with one style and one parting placed Target ¶ Pick your head mesh here. Only mesh objects can be picked. Its tooltip reads: Mesh to stamp partings onto. Leave empty to use the active object. You can leave it empty. The panel then works on the mesh you have selected and shows Active: followed by its name. With Target empty and no mesh selected, the panel shows "Pick a mesh, or select one". Everything below it is hidden, including Place Parting . Material And Slot Line ¶ Once the head has a parting, a line appears under Target . It names the partings material and the material slot it sits in. For example: Material.001_Partings · slot 0 . It is information only. Style ¶ The styles sit in their own Style box under Target , once the head has a style. A style is a complete set of partings on one head. Each style gets its own row, listed in alphabetical order. The style showing on the head has a filled dot and a highlighted row. The first style on a head is called Style 1 . Select another style's row to load it. The style that was showing is parked: its partings come off the head and their Empties are hidden. A parked style stays in your file, ready to load again. When a style loads, the status bar says how many of its partings are showing. For example: Loaded 'Style 1' — 1 parting(s) shown. Turn Preview Off First Select Disable Preview before you load another style or use New Style… . With Preview on, the style you load can come back with its partings' Empties hidden. A parting you hid stays hidden when its style loads again. Pencil (Rename Style) ¶ The pencil at the right of a style's row renames that style. Type the new name in the Name field and confirm. Each style on a head needs its own name, and capitals don't count. With Style 1 on the head, the name "style 1" is refused. Renaming a style also renames its collection in the Outliner. Trash (Delete Style) ¶ The trash can at the right of a style's row deletes that style, along with its partings and their Empties. The trash can is greyed out while the head has only one style. To clear the last style, use Reset Partings . Blender asks you to confirm first. Pressed it by mistake? Ctrl+Z straight after brings the style back, partings included. New Style… ¶ Parks the style you have now and gives you an empty one to place into. It stays greyed out until the current style has at least one parting. A dialog called New Parting Style opens with two names filled in: Field What it names Name Current The style being parked, for example Style 1 New Style The empty style you are about to place into, for example Style 2 Select Continue . The two names must differ, and neither can match another style on the head. The status bar confirms it, for example Parked 'Style 1' (2 Empty(s) hidden). Now stamping into 'Style 2'. Place partings into the new style as usual. See Place Parting And Placement Keys . Parting Mask ¶ The Parting Mask box sits under the styles. It sets the image each new parting is stamped with. The thumbnail shows the mask new partings will use. Select it to pick from your masks. The list holds only masks: images added with + , and images your partings already use. With no mask picked, a line under the thumbnail says which image will be used. Using: bundled default means the mask that ships with the add-on. Its tooltip starts: Displacement map used for new stamps. Picking a mask only affects partings you place afterwards. To change partings already on the head, use Replace . To make your own mask, match the one that ships with the add-on: A square greyscale PNG, 1024 × 1024 pixels. White where the parting shows. Brighter areas show more strongly. Black around the edges. Anything past the edge of the image is cut off. Arrows ¶ The two arrows beside the label step back and forward through your masks. They wrap round at the ends. Their tooltip reads: Step to the previous or next parting mask. Plus (Add Parting Mask) ¶ The + loads a mask from an image file. The image is packed into the .blend, so the file keeps working if the image moves. It stays in the file even when no parting uses it. Its tooltip reads: Load an image as a parting mask for new partings. It is packed into the .blend and set to sRGB. Trash (Remove From Masks) ¶ The trash can takes the shown mask out of your list. Partings already using it keep it, and it stays listed until they are replaced. A mask nothing uses is dropped from the file the next time you save. Its tooltip reads: Take the current Parting Mask out of the mask list. Partings already using it keep it. Replace ¶ Shown at the bottom of the box once the head has partings. It puts the shown mask on the ticked partings, or on the highlighted one when nothing is ticked. Position, shape, warp and settings stay as they were. Linked mirrors follow. The button names what it will change, for example Replace on Parting 002 or Replace on 3 Ticked . With nothing to change it reads Replace Mask and is greyed out. If Preview Mode is on, Replace turns it off so the new mask shows. It is greyed out while you are placing partings or editing a warp. Its tooltip then says Finish placing or warp editing first. Its tooltip reads: Put the current Parting Mask on the ticked partings (or the active one when none are ticked). Position, shape, warp and settings are kept. If You're Stuck Partings gone after you loaded a style? See I Cannot See Any Partings . Nothing appears when you place? See Place Parting Does Nothing . Anything else: Still Stuck . Recommended next: Place Parting And Placement Keys

docs.text: Applies to: Parting Placer V2.0.0 · Blender 4.4 · 5.2 This page covers the top of the panel. Target picks the head you are working on. Under it, the Style box holds that head's styles, and the Parting Mask box sets the image new partings use. The large Place Parting button sits below them. See Place Parting . [1] The top of the panel with one style and one parting placed
docs.title: Target And Styles

docs.text: Pick your head mesh here. Only mesh objects can be picked. Its tooltip reads: Mesh to stamp partings onto. Leave empty to use the active object. You can leave it empty. The panel then works on the mesh you have selected and shows Active: followed by its name. With Target empty and no mesh selected, the panel shows "Pick a mesh, or select one". Everything below it is hidden, including Place Parting .
docs.title: Target

docs.text: Once the head has a parting, a line appears under Target . It names the partings material and the material slot it sits in. For example: Material.001_Partings · slot 0 . It is information only.
docs.title: Material And Slot Line

docs.text: The styles sit in their own Style box under Target , once the head has a style. A style is a complete set of partings on one head. Each style gets its own row, listed in alphabetical order. The style showing on the head has a filled dot and a highlighted row. The first style on a head is called Style 1 . Select another style's row to load it. The style that was showing is parked: its partings come off the head and their Empties are hidden. A parked style stays in your file, ready to load again. When a style loads, the status bar says how many of its partings are showing. For example: Loaded 'Style 1' — 1 parting(s) shown. Turn Preview Off First Select Disable Preview before you load another style or use New Style… . With Preview on, the style you load can come back with its partings' Empties hidden. A parting you hid stays hidden when its style loads again.
docs.title: Style

docs.text: The pencil at the right of a style's row renames that style. Type the new name in the Name field and confirm. Each style on a head needs its own name, and capitals don't count. With Style 1 on the head, the name "style 1" is refused. Renaming a style also renames its collection in the Outliner.
docs.title: Pencil (Rename Style)

docs.text: The trash can at the right of a style's row deletes that style, along with its partings and their Empties. The trash can is greyed out while the head has only one style. To clear the last style, use Reset Partings . Blender asks you to confirm first. Pressed it by mistake? Ctrl+Z straight after brings the style back, partings included.
docs.title: Trash (Delete Style)

docs.text: Parks the style you have now and gives you an empty one to place into. It stays greyed out until the current style has at least one parting. A dialog called New Parting Style opens with two names filled in: Field What it names Name Current The style being parked, for example Style 1 New Style The empty style you are about to place into, for example Style 2 Select Continue . The two names must differ, and neither can match another style on the head. The status bar confirms it, for example Parked 'Style 1' (2 Empty(s) hidden). Now stamping into 'Style 2'. Place partings into the new style as usual. See Place Parting And Placement Keys .
docs.title: New Style…

docs.text: The Parting Mask box sits under the styles. It sets the image each new parting is stamped with. The thumbnail shows the mask new partings will use. Select it to pick from your masks. The list holds only masks: images added with + , and images your partings already use. With no mask picked, a line under the thumbnail says which image will be used. Using: bundled default means the mask that ships with the add-on. Its tooltip starts: Displacement map used for new stamps. Picking a mask only affects partings you place afterwards. To change partings already on the head, use Replace . To make your own mask, match the one that ships with the add-on: A square greyscale PNG, 1024 × 1024 pixels. White where the parting shows. Brighter areas show more strongly. Black around the edges. Anything past the edge of the image is cut off.
docs.title: Parting Mask

docs.text: The two arrows beside the label step back and forward through your masks. They wrap round at the ends. Their tooltip reads: Step to the previous or next parting mask.
docs.title: Arrows

docs.text: The + loads a mask from an image file. The image is packed into the .blend, so the file keeps working if the image moves. It stays in the file even when no parting uses it. Its tooltip reads: Load an image as a parting mask for new partings. It is packed into the .blend and set to sRGB.
docs.title: Plus (Add Parting Mask)

A mask nothing uses is dropped from the file the next time you save. Its tooltip reads: Take the current Parting Mask out of the mask list. Partings already using it keep it.
